claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances and the child or children you're enquiring about.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's just turned 17.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 17, his eligibility depends on his current situation with education or training.

**Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar), or on an approved training course?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he actually left school recently, but he's just signed up with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is helpful information.

Let me ask a bit more about Alex's situation:

**When did Alex leave school, and has he registered with the careers service or a similar organisation (such as Connexions, or a local authority careers advice service) for a place in education or training?**

I ask because there are specific rules about young people who have left education but are registered for training or further education.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He left school a few weeks ago, maybe about a month or so now. Yes, he registered with the careers service right after leaving - I think it's been about 3 or 4 weeks since he signed up with them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for those details. That's very helpful.

I have a couple more questions to make sure I have the full picture:

**Is Alex living with you, and are you responsible for his day-to-day care?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me and I look after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I've now reviewed the eligibility rules.

I have one more important question:

**Is Alex currently working 24 hours or more per week, receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance), or has he started an apprenticeship?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all right now - that's why he's with the careers service, trying to figure out his next steps. He's not getting any benefits either, and he hasn't started an apprenticeship.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming all of that. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 17 years old
- He left school about a month ago
- He registered with the careers service shortly after leaving (3-4 weeks ago)
- He lives with you and you are responsible for his care
- He is not working 24+ hours per week, not on an apprenticeship, and not receiving benefits in his own right

Let me now make my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of my assessment:

**For Alex (age 17):** ✅ Eligible

Since Alex is 16 or 17, has left education, and has registered with a government-sponsored careers service, you can claim Child Benefit for him for up to **20 weeks** from when he left school. This is a specific provision in the rules for young people in his situation.

**Important things to note:**
- This 20-week eligibility period runs from when Alex left education
- Your eligibility would end early if Alex:
  - Starts working 24 or more hours per week
  - Begins an apprenticeship (in England)
  - Starts receiving certain benefits like Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance

If Alex decides to return to approved full-time education or training (such as A-levels, a BTEC, or similar) before turning 20, you may continue to be eligible beyond this 20-week period.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about your Child Benefit eligibility?

Since Alex registered with the careers service within the appropriate timeframe after leaving education, his parent can claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks from when he left education, provided he remains registered and does not start work of 24+ hours, an apprenticeship, or claim certain benefits.
